flawed_step: The input contains no numbered proof steps. The universal assertion itself cannot be justified, because the explicit graph below satisfies every hypothesis but has no Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample:
Define a 15-vertex fragment F with vertices {p,q,s,t,a,b,c,d,e,u,v,w,x,y,r} and edges {pa,ab,bc,cs,sd,de,eq,qt,tp,tu,ay,bx,cr,dr,ev,uv,uy,vw,wx,wr,xy}. Thus p,q,s have degree 2 and every other vertex has degree 3. Take three disjoint indexed copies F_i (i=0,1,2), add a vertex o, and add the six edges os_i and q_i p_{i+1}, with indices modulo 3. This explicitly defines a simple graph G on 46 vertices.

Cubic: each formerly degree-2 port p_i,q_i,s_i receives exactly one new edge, and o has degree 3.

Planar: F has outer boundary cycle p-a-b-c-s-d-e-q-t-p. If a new hub h is joined to p,q,s, a planar embedding is certified by these ten facial cycles: (h,p,a,b,c,s), (h,s,d,e,q), (h,q,t,p), (p,a,y,u,t), (a,b,x,y), (b,c,r,w,x), (c,s,d,r), (d,e,v,w,r), (e,q,t,u,v), and (u,v,w,x,y). Replacing each of the three noncentral vertices of a planar K4 by this embedded fragment produces exactly G, so G is planar.

3-connected: the displayed facial embedding of F+h is polyhedral—every face boundary is a simple cycle and any two facial cycles meet only in an empty set, one vertex, or one edge—so F+h is 3-connected. Replacing a degree-3 vertex of a 3-connected graph by such a three-terminal fragment preserves 3-connectivity: after deletion of at most two vertices, every fragment component still meets a surviving terminal, while the K4 skeleton with at most two affected incidences remains connected. Applying this to the three noncentral vertices of K4 proves that G remains connected after deletion of any two vertices.

Non-Hamiltonian certificate: first, F has no spanning p-to-q path. Indeed, in such a path the internal degree-2 port s forces cs and sd. At t, exactly one of pt,qt is used and tu is forced. If pt is used, then qe,tu,ab,ay are forced. If uy is then used, degree propagation produces the disjoint 4-cycle c-s-d-r-c. If uv is used and ev is used, it produces the disjoint 9-cycle a-b-c-s-d-r-w-x-y-a; if uv is used and ev is omitted, it produces the disjoint 4-cycle a-b-x-y-a. If qt is used instead, degree propagation produces the disjoint 7-cycle c-s-d-e-v-w-r-c. Every case contradicts the existence of one spanning path.

Now suppose G had a Hamiltonian cycle C. For each fragment F_i, its three-edge boundary is {os_i, q_{i-1}p_i, q_i p_{i+1}}. A cycle crosses every cut evenly, so C uses exactly two of these three edges. At o, C uses exactly two of os_0,os_1,os_2; hence for the unique index j whose edge os_j is omitted, C must use both other boundary edges of F_j. The portion of C inside F_j would consequently be a spanning p_j-to-q_j path, which the preceding exhaustive forcing argument proves impossible. Therefore G is an explicit 3-connected cubic planar graph with no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: A concrete 46-vertex counterexample is given by three copies of the explicitly defined three-terminal fragment substituted into the three noncentral vertices of K4. Its cubicity, planarity, and 3-connectivity are certified structurally, and a complete local edge-forcing argument rules out every Hamiltonian cycle.
